claim_verdicts.evidence: Overview: "Argo CD is a declarative, GitOps continuous delivery tool for Kubernetes." Architecture: application controller "compares the current, live state against the desired target state (as specified in the repo)"; repo server is "responsible for generating and returning the Kubernetes manifests" (no component builds images). Core concepts, Sync: "E.g. by applying changes to a Kubernetes cluster." Pods: argocd-install.txt lists 6 deployment.apps + 1 statefulset.apps in argocd.

Getting Started: "kubectl create namespace argocd" then "kubectl apply -n argocd -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/argoproj/argo-cd/stable/manifests/install.yaml". Upgrading overview: "kubectl apply -n argocd -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/argoproj/argo-cd/<version>/manifests/install.yaml". deploy/argocd/install.yaml: images quay.io/argoproj/argocd:v3.1.16; Grep 'kind: Namespace|CustomResourceDefinition' = 3 hits, all CRDs (no Namespace).

Getting Started installs Argo CD with kubectl from outside the cluster (create namespace, apply install.yaml); no Argo CD component exists before that apply. argocd-install.sh:3 "Runs on the host, like scripts/k8s/"; :14 creates the namespace, :16 applies the manifest.

argocd-install.txt: "3 customresourcedefinition.apiextensions.k8s.io", "6 deployment.apps", "8 service", role/clusterrole bindings, "1 statefulset.apps"; deployments applicationset-controller, dex-server, notifications-controller, redis, repo-server, server; statefulset argocd-application-controller. K8s StatefulSet page: "A StatefulSet runs a group of Pods". Lesson output block = file lines 1-2, 6-7, 16-32 with '...' elisions.

argocd-install.txt: "applications app,apps argoproj.io/v1alpha1 true Application", plus applicationsets, appprojects (namespaced true). gitops-first-sync.txt:2 "application.argoproj.io/staging" after kubectl apply. K8s (refs, exact): "The API group is specified in a REST path and in the `apiVersion` field of a serialized object."; named groups "use `apiVersion: $GROUP_NAME/$VERSION`".

Architecture: "The repository server is an internal service which maintains a local cache of the Git repository holding the application manifests. It is responsible for generating and returning the Kubernetes manifests". "The application controller is a Kubernetes controller which continuously monitors running applications and compares the current, live state against the desired target state (as specified in the repo)."

Projects: "If unspecified, an application belongs to the `default` project, which is created automatically". Tracking strategies: branch -> "compare live state against the resource manifests defined at the tip of the specified branch"; commit SHA -> "the app is effectively pinned to the manifests defined at the specified commit." Declarative Setup minimal Application: project: default; source repoURL/targetRevision/path; destination server/namespace.

K8s (refs, exact): "The API server's in-cluster address is also published to a Service named `kubernetes` in the `default` namespace so that pods may reference `kubernetes.default.svc` as a DNS name for the local API server." Argo CD Declarative Setup example uses "server: https://kubernetes.default.svc" as destination.

Declarative Setup: "All resources, including `Application` and `AppProject` specs, have to be installed in the Argo CD namespace"; "The namespace must match the namespace of your Argo CD instance - typically this is `argocd`." Apps in any namespace (namespaces "other than the control plane's namespace"): "this feature has to be explicitly enabled and configured appropriately."

Auto sync page: automated sync is enabled by "a syncPolicy with an `automated` policy" (example spec.syncPolicy.automated: {}). Execution: after applying staging-manual.yaml (no syncPolicy), gitops-first-sync.txt:3 shows "staging: OutOfSync, Missing" and every resource OutOfSync until the script explicitly requests "== sync" (line 26). Core concepts, Refresh: "Compare the latest code in Git with the live state."

Directory apps: "By default, directory applications will only include the files from the root of the configured repository/path." staging-manual.yaml:17 path: envs/staging. gitops-first-sync.txt lists only staging's objects (SealedSecret/* exist only under envs/staging per gitops-repo.txt). gitops-repo.sh:54-58 copies only apps/staging.yaml.

git-server.yaml: Namespace git; Deployment gitea replicas: 1; volume data emptyDir mounted /var/lib/gitea; Service gitea (no type, i.e. ClusterIP) port 3000; ROOT_URL http://gitea.git.svc:3000/. K8s volumes (refs, exact): "When a Pod is removed from a node for any reason, the data in the `emptyDir` is deleted permanently."

gitops-repo.sh:46-48 "The first commit: the folders of deploy/gitops/config-repo, and for envs/staging the SealedSecrets that scripts/devops/seal-secrets.sh makes from .env"; :56-58 copy envs/ and apps/staging.yaml only; :59 seal-secrets.sh --no-commit; :61 "private":false; :63 config_commit. gitops-repo.txt:28-34 lists the 7 envs/staging/sealed-*.yaml; all files .yaml. Round 2: claim text and lesson sentence now include the sealed files.

Private Repositories: "If application manifests are located in private repository then repository credentials have to be configured." Execution: gitops-repo.sh:61 creates the repo with "private":false; no Secret with argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type exists anywhere in examples/don-hang (Grep, install.yaml excluded); yet gitops-first-sync.txt shows Argo CD reading envs/staging.

envs/staging/api.yaml:42 "image: ghcr.io/duyan11110/donhang-api:sha-bb184243e4cafed6ae833ca61710608366214aa5"; ci.yml:255-256 `docker tag "$LOCAL" "$name:sha-$GITHUB_SHA"` / `docker push`. Other images in envs/staging are public tags (postgres:17.6-alpine, redis:8.10.2-alpine, quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.7.4, axllent/mailpit:v1.31.3).

gitops-first-sync.sh:16 `kubectl apply -f deploy/gitops/lessons/staging-manual.yaml -o name` -> gitops-first-sync.txt:2 "application.argoproj.io/staging". argocd-install.txt: every workload in argocd is named argocd-* (6 deployments + statefulset argocd-application-controller), so no Pod named staging.

kind Quick Start: "you only need to specify the cluster name as a context in kubectl" with `kubectl cluster-info --context kind-kind`. deploy/tofu/modules/kind-cluster/main.tf:8 source "tehcyx/kind", :14 resource kind_cluster; variables.tf:5 "Name of the kind cluster; its kubectl context is kind-<name>." argocd-install.sh:7, scripts/lib/gitops.sh:7: `kubectl() { command kubectl --context kind-donhang-staging "$@"; }`; gitops-repo.sh:12 sources gitops.sh.

kubectl apply (refs): "This resource will be created if it doesn't exist yet." create --dry-run: "If client strategy, only print the object that would be sent, without sending it." rollout status: "watch the status of the latest rollout until it's done." Code blocks compared char-for-char with examples/don-hang working tree in round 1; unchanged in round 2. Prose now names lines by command, matching the code.

issues.text: New in round 2 (changed sentence). gitops-repo.sh:54-58 copies only envs/ and apps/staging.yaml; deploy/gitops/config-repo also holds apps/edge-staging.yaml, apps/policies-staging.yaml, apps/traefik.yaml and platform/, which are not pushed ("the other Applications and platform/ are added by the k8s lessons that use them"), and :59 adds the sealed-*.yaml files. "the contents of" contradicts section 5 and the printed file list.
issues.quote: pushes the contents of `deploy/gitops/config-repo` to it as a new repository, `donhang-config`
issues.fix: Replace "pushes the contents of `deploy/gitops/config-repo` to it" with "pushes manifests from `deploy/gitops/config-repo` to it" (section 5 already lists exactly which). Keep the rest of the sentence.

issues.text: New in round 2 (changed option b). From section 2 I reject b because pointing at all of `envs` would mix staging's files with production's. The explanation gives a different reason, that an Application reads only the files directly in the folder it names, not in folders below it. The lesson never says that, so the explanation adds a rule I cannot check and makes me doubt my own reasoning.
issues.quote: But an Application reads the manifests of exactly the folder it names; `envs` holds only the folders of the two environments, not staging's manifests
issues.fix: Base the b explanation on what section 2 says: 'But `envs` also holds production's folder, and an Application pointed at it could not tell staging's files from production's; name `envs/staging`.'
